findings.title: retryCount never incremented when message or sendTo is empty, so the new retry/delete mechanism is bypassed
findings.body: The new retry/delete behavior only fires inside the branches that actually attempt scheduling. When `message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo` is falsy (e.g. SMS template evaluates to an empty string, attendee has no phone number, etc.) the entire `if` block is skipped, no `twilio.scheduleSMS` call is made, and neither the `else` (line 179) nor the `catch` (line 190) path runs. The reminder therefore never has its `retryCount` incremented and will be picked up again on every cron run until its `scheduledDate` passes, exactly the bug this PR claims to fix. The PR description's stated goal is to delete reminders that fail to schedule after two attempts, so empty message / missing recipient must also drive `retryCount` (e.g. increment in an `else` for the outer guard) or be deleted immediately.

findings.title: Cleanup deleteMany applies retryCount > 1 to non-SMS reminders too
findings.body: The new cleanup `deleteMany` uses an `OR` whose second branch is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first branch. The first branch is correctly scoped to SMS, but the second branch will delete any `WorkflowReminder` row (including EMAIL and WHATSAPP) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1, regardless of scheduledDate. Today only this SMS path increments `retryCount`, but any future change that bumps the counter for email/whatsapp (or a stray backfill) will silently delete those reminders too. The retryCount clause should be `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 }` to keep semantics consistent with the rest of the handler.

findings.title: retryCount increment is read-modify-write and not atomic
findings.body: The update uses `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`, where `reminder.retryCount` was read earlier in `findMany`. If two cron invocations (or any concurrent process) process the same reminder, both will read the same value and both will write `value + 1`, silently losing one retry attempt and possibly keeping a failing reminder alive beyond the intended two attempts. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation (e.g. `update({ where: { id }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })`) in both the `else` branch (line 179-186) and the `catch` branch (line 190-197).

findings.title: SMS scheduling errors are logged with console.log instead of console.error
findings.body: The catch block at line 198 uses `console.log(`Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`)`. Failure logs should use `console.error` so they are routed to error streams/aggregators and don't get buried in routine info output; otherwise on-call engineers triaging SMS delivery issues have to grep for the string "Error scheduling" in info-level logs.

findings.title: No tests added for the new retryCount / cleanup behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a new `retryCount` column, a new cleanup branch in `deleteMany` (`retryCount > 1`), and new increment paths in both the `else` and `catch` branches. None of these are covered by automated tests. Given there are several failure paths (twilio returns falsy, twilio throws, message empty, sendTo missing) and a non-trivial boundary (`gt: 1` rather than `gte: 1`), this is a regression risk. Tests should at minimum cover: SMS scheduled successfully -> `scheduled: true` set; twilio returns falsy -> `retryCount` becomes 1, reminder still present; twilio throws -> `retryCount` becomes 1; reminder with `retryCount >= 2` is deleted by the cleanup `deleteMany`; the empty message / missing sendTo case actually increments `retryCount` (or is fixed to do so per the other finding).
